note: Build an initial three-column plant targeting the two most valuable easily defined blends, while measuring the difficult C6 paraffin/naphthene separation.
notebook:
PLAN: (1) Establish a high-value skeleton recovering C5 and C6-paraffin blends, (2) inspect splits/costs and tune difficult C6 cut, (3) add only profitable recovery of C4/C3 and heavy products, (4) optimize energy/stages and compare peer designs.
Initial 3-column design: root separates C5- overhead from C6+; T splits C4- from saleable C5 blend; B makes the difficult N-hexane/methylcyclopentane cut to sell the very valuable C6 paraffin blend. C5 and C6 paraffin blends have nominal revenues about $611M/yr and $1147M/yr, so they dominate early value.

note: Reconfigure the same three columns into a direct C4/C5/C6+ sequence and sharpen all three splits to obtain the first positive-revenue design.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Establish a profitable 3-column skeleton selling C4 and C5 blends, (2) add C3 recovery if ethane can be removed cheaply, (3) add high-value C6-paraffin recovery only if purity/cost justify it, (4) optimize settings and compare peers. Step 1 now: sharpen root C4/C5 split, T C3/C4 split, and B C5/C6 split. Initial R=3 root cut inside C5 and all products failed; C5 blend nominal $611M/yr and C4 $154M/yr should support this skeleton.

note: Test much sharper C4/C5 and C5/C6 splits at higher pressure drops; the first priority is to obtain the two valuable sellable blend streams.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Establish a profitable 3-column skeleton selling C4 and C5 blends, (2) add C3 recovery if ethane can be removed cheaply, (3) add high-value C6-paraffin recovery only if purity/cost justify it, (4) optimize settings and compare peers. Step 1: make genuinely sharp C4/C5 and C5/C6 cuts. First two designs showed R/B 3-6 and 40-60 stages leave every blend far below 95%; root at 60/6 put 450 mol/s C5 overhead and B at 60/5 left 23% C5 in its tops. Now test 70 stages and R/B=12, with 0.30-0.35 pressure drop to improve volatility and reduce refrigeration. Target TB=C4 blend ($154M/yr), BT=C5 blend ($611M/yr); TT and BB remain unsold. If revenue appears, reduce stages/ratios and pressure costs systematically.

note: Cut energy and pressure costs sharply while strengthening only the C4/C5 split, whose 12% N-butane contamination is blocking $618M/yr of C5-blend revenue.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Establish a profitable 3-column skeleton selling C5 and C6-paraffin blends, (2) add C3/C4 recovery only if incremental value exceeds cost, (3) optimize stages, reflux and pressure. Step 1 now: retain the successful root/B C6 cut, sharpen T enough to push residual N-butane out of TB, and slash pressure drops and duties. Current BT already earns $1122M/yr; TB is 88% C5 with 12% N-butane, so it is the closest extra $618M/yr. TT is far from C4 spec and can remain unsold. Peer data show 70/8/dp.15 root costs $456M versus my 70/12/dp.35 at $748M, confirming aggressive pressure drop and ratios are uneconomic. Test root/B 60/8/dp.15 and T 80/14/dp.15; then relax whichever split has margin.

note: Make one decisive C4/C5 split at higher pressure, where relative volatility is better, to unlock the C5 blend; the cheap C6-producing root and B columns remain unchanged.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Establish a profitable 3-column skeleton selling C5 and C6-paraffin blends, (2) add C3/C4 recovery only if incremental value exceeds cost, (3) optimize stages, reflux and pressure. Step 1: root/B at 60/8/dp.15 preserve the $1122M/yr C6 blend cheaply; T must remove N-butane from TB. Lowering T pressure to dp.15 badly hurt relative volatility (TB fell to 76% C5), whereas peer dp.4 reached 90%. Test a decisive T=110 stages, R=B=24, dp.35 to exceed 95%, then relax aggressively once saleable. Avoid further low-pressure sharpening attempts: saved utilities are outweighed by lost C5 revenue.

note: Adopt the island's proven profitable four-column skeleton before optimizing its expensive root and C6 splitter.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Adopt the proven four-column C5/C6-paraffin/N-butane skeleton, (2) reduce root and C6-splitter costs while protecting blend specifications, (3) test cheaper light-end recovery and prune if uneconomic. Step 1: copy R209, which earns $1865.6M/yr at reward 1.555. Its root 70/8/9/dp.25 and B 90/11/11/dp.1 jointly deliver 96% C5 and 98% C6-paraffin; my extreme-reflux T column was much more expensive and still failed. Preserve these splits initially. The TT column adds $149.6M revenue for $93.7M cost, so retain it for now.

note: Trim the two dominant column costs moderately while preserving the demonstrated blend splits and light-end column settings.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Adopt the proven four-column C5/C6-paraffin/N-butane skeleton, (2) reduce root and C6-splitter costs while protecting blend specifications, (3) test cheaper light-end recovery and prune if uneconomic. Step 2: baseline R209 gives reward 1.555, revenue $1865.6M and cost $1183.6M. Root costs $515.9M and B $392.3M, dominating cost. C5 blend has 4% n-butane and C6 blend only ~2% naphthene +1% pentane, so some purity margin exists. Test moderate reductions to root 65/7.5/8.5 and B 75/9/9 at unchanged pressures; retain T and TT. If either blend drops below 95%, revert and relax only the failing split.

PLAN: (1) Adopt the proven four-column C5/C6-paraffin/N-butane skeleton, (2) reduce root and C6-splitter costs while protecting blend specifications, (3) test cheaper light-end recovery and prune if uneconomic. Step 3: current reward 1.711; root and B now cost $488.7M and $325.2M and both blends sell. TT costs $93.4M to recover only $149.0M of N-butane, leaving $55.6M net. Test a much smaller TT (40 stages, R=4, boil-up=6) while retaining its pressure; 99% current purity gives room to cut cost. If it falls below 95%, selling TTT directly is better than the present TT by about $56M/yr, but an optimized TT may still be worthwhile. Do not weaken root/B further without evidence: R306 shows root 60/6/7 destroys both blends.

note: Push the now-profitable N-butane column modestly further toward its minimum-cost 95% specification while leaving the validated blend splits unchanged.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Adopt the proven four-column C5/C6-paraffin/N-butane skeleton, (2) reduce root and C6-splitter costs while protecting blend specifications, (3) optimize the light-end recovery. Step 3: current best 1.742 with TT 40/4/6 producing 96% N-butane and costing $64M; it nets about $69M, so retain a TT rather than sell TTT. Test TT 35/3.5/5.5 to see whether its 95% specification survives a further cut. Root 65/7.5/8.5 and B 75/9/9 are fragile: reducing root to 60/7/8 destroys C6, and B 70 saves almost nothing. T is the next cost target after TT.

note: Adopt the island-best design and reduce only the C5 splitter's reflux: its tops are an intermediate, so retaining boil-up should preserve C5 purity at lower energy cost.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Adopt island-best R399 (B 75/8.5/8.5 and TT 40/4/6), (2) cut reflux where only one outlet must meet specification, (3) retune TT and root if worthwhile. Step 2: test T at 60/4.5/8 rather than 6/8. Its tops need not be pure; maintaining boil-up should protect the valuable C5 bottoms while lower reflux cuts cost. R399 is the safe fallback at 1.770. B has only about 1% C6-blend purity slack, so avoid across-the-board cuts there; root reductions previously destroyed C6 sales. Premium TT at 60/8/9 nets less than R399's cheap 96% N-butane column.

note: Restore the island-best design and make one further small, isolated reduction in the C6 splitter's energy use, where the last reduction was profitable and some blend-purity margin remains.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Restore island-best R449 (reward 1.796), (2) continue isolated C6-splitter energy reduction while monitoring blend purity, (3) test small root/T/TT savings if margin remains. Step 2: B at 8.0/8.0 saved about $17M/yr versus 8.5 while losing only $5M/yr revenue; its C6 blend has roughly 1.8 percentage-point purity slack. Test 7.75/7.75. Avoid repeating the failed T reflux cut to 4.5, which lost both C5 and N-butane sales. Root reductions previously damaged C6 sales, so preserve R449 as fallback.

note: Reduce only the C6 splitter's boil-up: bottoms are unsold, while maintaining reflux should protect the marginal tops blend purity better than another symmetric cut.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Preserve the 1.808 design, (2) reduce C6-splitter cost asymmetrically now that symmetric 7.5/7.5 is known to fail, (3) then test small TT savings. Step 2: B at 7.75/7.75 sells the C6 blend at essentially the 95% boundary; 7.5/7.5 loses it. Since only BT must meet specification and BB is unsold, retain reflux for tops purity while cutting only boil-up to 7.25. Root duty trimming previously failed convergence or damaged sales; T reflux trimming also failed. Revert immediately if BT falls below specification.

note: Restore the best design and test a double-effect root: its very large heat duty offers the clearest remaining opportunity for a material saving without changing any product split.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Preserve R496 at 1.808, (2) test heat integration on the dominant $488.7M/yr root, (3) if that fails return to R496 and make small TT/root energy optimizations. Step 2: asymmetric B trimming lost $30M revenue to save only $9M, so retain B 75/7.75/7.75. The root handles 3300 mol/s and dominates cost; a 50/50 double effect at 18/12 bar may allow its HP condenser to drive the LP reboiler. Downstream settings remain unchanged. A taller low-duty root failed convergence; avoid that direction.

note: Restore the validated best plant and test a modest five-stage reduction only in the C6 splitter, holding its reflux and boil-up fixed to protect the marginal blend.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Restore R496 at 1.808, (2) make isolated capital/energy trims with immediate reversion on purity loss, (3) use remaining solves for the most promising root/T changes. Step 2: test B at 70 stages with unchanged ratios; this targets its $283M/yr cost while retaining the demonstrated C6 split. Prior results: B boil-up 7.5 cost revenue and scored 1.760; T boil-up 7.75 and root energy reduction each destroyed a blend. Root double effect failed convergence. R496 remains the fallback: C5 and C6 blends have only modest purity margins, so avoid simultaneous changes.

note: Adopt the slightly better 1.809 plant and trim only the root from 65 to 60 stages, retaining its energy settings to test capital savings without intentionally changing the split.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Adopt R645 (1.809) with its validated 55-stage T column, (2) cautiously trim root capital, the largest cost centre, while holding its energy and cut controls fixed, (3) revert immediately if either blend loses specification and then test only small isolated changes. Step 2: root 65 to 60 stages. R496/R645 show B=75 is needed: B=70 lost the C6 blend, while B boil-up 7.5 also hurt. T=55 retained C5 purity. Root double effect failed and root dp=0.4 raised root cost and caused downstream failure. Preserve B=75, T=55/6/8/0.2, TT=40/4/6/0.2 as fallback.

note: Restore the fully validated R691 plant and make one small reduction in the dominant root column's boil-up, holding its cut pressure and reflux fixed to test energy savings while protecting both blend specifications.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Restore R691, the validated 1.809 plant with cheaper 50-stage T and 35-stage TT columns, (2) reduce only root energy in small steps because its $488.7M/yr cost dominates, (3) retain the best valid plant and stop if blend purity deteriorates. Step 2: root boil-up 8.5 to 8.25, holding reflux and pressure fixed. R691 saves about $0.7M/yr versus R645 while preserving both blends and 96% N-butane. Root 60 stages fails, double effect fails, and higher pressure drop is worse; B=75 and its energy settings are necessary for the C6 blend. Preserve R691 settings as fallback: root 65/7.5/8.5/0.25, B 75/7.75/7.75/0.1, T 50/6/8/0.2, TT 35/4/6/0.2.

note: Restore the 1.811 plant and reduce only the terminal N-butane column from 35 to 30 stages; its 96% product has a modest purity margin and unchanged energy settings should preserve the cut.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Use R737 as the validated 1.811 fallback, (2) trim the terminal N-butane column in five-stage increments while retaining its energy settings, (3) test B pressure or root energy only if the terminal trim stalls, and keep the best valid design. Step 2: TT 35 to 30 stages. R737's B dp=0.2 raises C6 recovery enough to offset its higher cost; T=55 and TT=35 preserve 96% N-butane. Root 60 stages, boil-up 8.25 and double effect all fail; B boil-up reduction loses blend value. Fallback R737: root 65/7.5/8.5/0.25, B 75/7.75/7.75/0.2, T 55/6/8/0.2, TT 35/4/6/0.2.

note: Use the island-best 55-stage terminal column and raise only its reflux modestly: its 97% N-butane is close enough that a small energy increase may reach the valuable 99% premium.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Adopt R787 as the 1.813 fallback, (2) increase TT reflux modestly to seek 99% N-butane premium while retaining its validated 55-stage separation, (3) if premium is not reached, revert and test pressure or a targeted root/B energy trim. Step 2: TT reflux 4.0 to 4.5. R787 gains $6M/yr versus 35 stages and $1.5M/yr net. TT at 30 stages falls to 95%, so stage cuts are exhausted. Root 60 stages, boil-up 8.25 and double effect fail; B boil-up cuts lose blend value; BB recovery is uneconomic. Fallback R787: root 65/7.5/8.5/0.25, B 75/7.75/7.75/0.2, T 55/6/8/0.2, TT 55/4/6/0.2.

note: Adopt the 1.830 plant and raise only terminal reflux: 70 stages already reach 98% N-butane, so a small increase may cross the valuable 99% premium threshold.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Adopt R833 as the 1.830 fallback, (2) push only the inexpensive terminal column toward 99% N-butane, (3) if premium remains out of reach, revert and test a small root/B energy trim. Step 2: raise TT reflux from 5.0 to 5.5 at 70 stages. R833 reaches 98% and earns $147.6M/yr; premium would add about $30M/yr revenue for little cost. TT stage cuts are exhausted, B boil-up cuts lose blend value, root 60 stages and boil-up 8.25 fail, and BB recovery is uneconomic. Fallback R833: root 65/7.5/8.5/0.25, B 75/7.75/7.75/0.2, T 55/6/8/0.2, TT 70/5/6/0.2.

note: Adopt the 1.838 plant and increase only terminal boil-up: stronger stripping should raise both N-butane purity and recovery, while leaving the validated blend splits untouched.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Adopt R880 as the 1.838 fallback, (2) use remaining solves on the inexpensive terminal N-butane column, then (3) revert to the best if no improvement. Step 2: raise TT boil-up from 6.0 to 6.5 at reflux 6.0 and 70 stages. R880 earns $154.4M/yr from 96% N-butane with 436 mol/s product; more boil-up should improve stripping of light components and recovery, potentially approaching the 99% premium. Root 60 stages and boil-up 8.25 fail; B boil-up cuts lose blend value; BB recovery is uneconomic. Fallback: root 65/7.5/8.5/0.25, B 75/7.75/7.75/0.2, T 55/6/8/0.2, TT 70/6/6/0.2.

note: Restore R880 and trim only the terminal column by five stages, checking whether its modest purity margin can fund a capital saving.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Preserve R880 (1.838) as fallback, (2) spend remaining solves on isolated terminal N-butane cost/purity tests, (3) revert if worse. Step 2: test TT 65/6/6; reducing five stages may retain the 95% specification and save capital without the purity/recovery losses seen at higher boil-up. R880 terminal 70/6/6 gives 96% N-butane, 436 mol/s, $154.4M/yr and costs $74.1M/yr. Boil-up 6.5 worsens reward to 1.824; reflux 6.25 and 7.0 also underperform. Root and C6 energy cuts fail or lose blend value. Fallback: root 65/7.5/8.5/0.25, B 75/7.75/7.75/0.2, T 55/6/8/0.2, TT 70/6/6/0.2.

note: Test a C4-mix bottoms product: reducing only terminal boil-up should retain isobutane with n-butane, potentially raising product value while lowering energy cost.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Preserve the 1.838 four-column backbone, (2) use remaining solves to test whether TT can sell the whole C4 blend instead of only n-butane, (3) retain the best validated terminal settings. Step 2: reduce only TT boil-up to 4.5 so isobutane remains in the bottoms while propane/propylene are rejected overhead; a 95% C4 blend could be worth up to about $186M/yr versus $154M/yr now, with lower duty. Root and C6 cuts have already failed or lost value. Fallback: root 65/7.5/8.5/0.25, B 75/7.75/7.75/0.2, T 55/6/8/0.2, TT 65/6/6/0.2.

notebook: PLAN: (1) Preserve the 1.877 four-column backbone, (2) optimize the terminal C4-mix cut with isolated boil-up changes, (3) retain the best validated settings. Step 2: test TT boil-up 4.0 after 4.5 yielded a fully qualifying 489 mol/s C4 blend worth $167.6M/yr. Lower boil-up may recover more isobutane and n-butane while the current zero light/heavy contamination provides purity margin. Root and C6 changes have failed or lost value. Fallback: root 65/7.5/8.5/0.25, B 75/7.75/7.75/0.2, T 55/6/8/0.2, TT 65/6/4.5/0.2.

note: Restore the validated 1.877 plant and test a shorter terminal column: its C4 blend has ample purity margin, so ten fewer stages may reduce capital without changing the product value.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Preserve the 1.877 four-column backbone, (2) reduce terminal-column capital while retaining its robust C4 blend, (3) retain the best validated settings. Step 2: restore TT boil-up 4.5 and test 55 stages instead of 65. The C4 blend has zero measurable contamination and does not require the high purity needed by the earlier pure n-butane product, so ten fewer stages may save capital without sacrificing revenue. Boil-up 4.0 failed to converge; do not repeat. Fallback: root 65/7.5/8.5/0.25, B 75/7.75/7.75/0.2, T 55/6/8/0.2, TT 65/6/4.5/0.2.

notebook: PLAN: (1) Adopt R1077's validated 1.884 backbone, (2) reduce terminal reflux while retaining boil-up 4.3 and its zero-contaminant C4 blend, (3) preserve the best validated result. Step 2: test TT reflux 5.5 rather than 6.0. R1077 gains $2.6M/yr over the current plant by increasing C4 recovery at boil-up 4.3. Its bottoms remain entirely C4, so modestly lower reflux may cut condenser duty without losing blend qualification. Boil-up 4.25 and 4.0 failed; do not reduce boil-up further. Root stage reductions also failed.

The C4 bottoms remains entirely C4, so five fewer stages may save capital without affecting blend qualification. Avoid boil-up reductions: 4.25 and 4.0 failed; root and heavy-column stage reductions also failed or lost value.

note: Trim the terminal C4 column by another five stages; its bottoms are entirely C4 with ample blend-purity margin, so this may save capital without changing recovery.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Preserve the validated 1.885 four-column backbone, (2) use remaining solves to trim only the terminal C4 column, where the blend has large purity margin, (3) stop if recovery or qualification deteriorates. Step 2: test TT at 45 stages after 50 stages retained essentially the same reward. Root duty reductions and heavy-column stage cuts have failed or lost value; terminal reflux 5.75 merely traded revenue for cost. Avoid touching the converged root, T, or B settings.

PLAN: (1) Adopt the clearly superior R1157 backbone at 1.936, (2) use remaining solves only for modest root-reflux reductions, which improved both cost and revenue at 7.25, (3) stop immediately if blend qualification or net reward worsens.
